title: Chou Farci
subtitle: Savoy cabbage leaves stuffed with pork, rice and herbs
excerpt: Blanched savoy leaves wrapped around a herbed pork and rice filling, then braised slowly in tomato and stock. A filling French country dish that reheats well.
sourceNotes: French farmhouse tradition; braised stuffed cabbage common across Auvergne and Burgundy.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool completely. Freeze in the braising liquid. Reheat gently on the hob, covered.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make a day ahead and reheat slowly on the hob. The flavour improves overnight.

content.text: Chou farci is a French braised cabbage parcel filled with herbed minced pork and rice. The long, slow cook in stock makes the leaves silky and the filling tender. Do not skip blanching the leaves or they will tear when you try to roll them.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Blanch the cabbage leaves for 2 minutes until pliable. Drain and spread flat on a clean surface to cool.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan. Soften the onion for 8 minutes over a medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute more. Leave to cool.
Mix the pork mince, rice, parsley, thyme, beaten egg and cooled onion in a bowl. Season with salt and black pepper. Mix well with your hands.
Heat the oven to 180C. Place 2 tablespoons of filling at the base of each leaf. Fold in the sides and roll up firmly into a parcel. Repeat with all the leaves and filling.
Place the parcels side by side in a roasting tin, seam-side down. They should sit snugly so they do not open during cooking.
Pour the tinned tomatoes and beef stock over the parcels. Cover the tin tightly with foil.
Braise in the oven for 75 minutes. The rice should be cooked through and the leaves very tender. Serve with the braising juices spooned over.

items.cause: The rolls were not tight enough, or were not placed seam-side down.
items.fix: Pack the parcels closely together in the tin so they hold each other in place.

items.symptom: The rice is still firm after baking.
items.cause: There was not enough liquid or the foil was not sealed tightly.
items.fix: Add an extra 100ml of stock, re-cover tightly and return to the oven for 20 minutes.

items.symptom: The cabbage leaves tore when rolling.
items.cause: The leaves were not blanched long enough, or the rib was too thick.
items.fix: Blanch for 3 minutes next time and use a knife to shave down any thick central ribs before rolling.
